findings.F1: In agitated markets the next-day rebound after a one-day fall is convex, not linear. Regressing the next-day excess return on the fall (in 30-day swings) and its square, falls only, t clustered by day: fall² +0.0124 (t 5.94), fall −0.0223 (t −2.76).
findings.F2: Only the deepest agitated falls carry that rebound. Next-day excess return, day-clustered:
findings.F3: The rebound after deep agitated falls also shows over two days and after three-day falls:
findings.F4: Contrary to the brief, calm markets also show a graded next-day rebound after falls. Among calm falls the linear slope is +0.0150 (t 2.64, day-clustered); calm falls of 1 to 1.5 swings return +0.77 % (t 1.94, 138 days). By year this is uneven: 2018 +0.16 %, 2019 +0.23 %, 2020 +1.66 % (t 3.14), 2021 +1.12 %.
findings.F5: In agitated markets, ordinary days within one usual swing are partly reversed the next day, and in calm markets they are not.
findings.F6: Rebounds after falls closing in the lowest quarter of their range look stronger, but not reliably once cases of one day are taken together. Falls beyond 1.5 swings closing low: agitated +2.52 % (t 2.06, 51 days) against +2.05 % (t 1.65) for the others; calm +0.82 % (t 1.23).
findings.F7: Falls beyond one swing made on a Thursday rebound +2.70 % the next day (t 2.66, 41 days), against +0.32 % to +0.45 % on other weekdays (t ≤ 1.1). This is one of seven weekdays checked and no single year reaches t 2, so it is not used for an idea.
findings.F8: The book earned +0.045 % a day over 1449 days, with 1 % tails of −2.05 % and +2.80 %. Window means range from −0.011 % to +0.179 %, so a few windows (w11, w14, w18) carry most of the gain, consistent with a profit concentrated in rare deep-fall days (F2).

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, a coin's next-day rise after a one-day fall grows faster than the fall itself, measured against its 30-day daily swing. A fall of a few usual swings is followed by a rise many times larger than a fall of about one swing, which is followed by almost none.
ideas.consequence: In agitated markets a trader should size a rebound bet steeply with the depth of the fall, putting almost all of it on the rare extreme falls whose rebound far exceeds a trade's cost.
ideas.name: agitated extreme fall convex rebound

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against its 30-day daily swing, the larger its rise over the next two days, growing faster than the fall.
ideas.consequence: Holding the rebound after a deep agitated fall for two days instead of one captures a larger move against a single trade's cost.
ideas.name: agitated deep fall two-day rebound

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's three-day fall measured against its 30-day daily swing, the larger its rise over the next day, growing faster than the fall.
ideas.consequence: A sharp multi-day slide in an agitated market is a reason to buy for a next-day rebound, more strongly the deeper the slide.
ideas.name: agitated three-day fall rebound

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall measured against its 30-day daily swing, the larger its rise over the next day, in calm as in agitated markets.
ideas.consequence: A rebound bet after scaled falls need not be confined to agitated markets, which would give it more days in a position.
ideas.name: scaled fall rebound every market

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, a coin's ordinary one-day rise is partly given back the next day, and the larger the rise within its usual daily swing, the larger the give-back.
ideas.consequence: In agitated markets a trader should not chase routine up days; they tend to reverse the next day.
ideas.name: agitated ordinary rise gives back
